input: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and how does it improve LLM outputs?
expected_output: RAG is a technique that enhances large language model responses by retrieving relevant documents from an external knowledge base before generating answers. It reduces hallucinations by grounding outputs in factual retrieved content, improves accuracy on domain-specific questions, and allows updating knowledge without retraining the model.

input: Compare different chunking strategies for RAG pipelines: fixed-size, recursive, and semantic chunking.
expected_output: Fixed-size chunking splits text at fixed token/character boundaries, which is simple but may break semantic units. Recursive chunking uses hierarchical separators (paragraphs, sentences, words) to preserve meaning better. Semantic chunking groups sentences by embedding similarity, producing coherent chunks but at higher computational cost. Recursive chunking offers the best balance of quality and performance for most RAG applications.

input: How do multi-agent systems with a supervisor pattern coordinate specialized sub-agents?
expected_output: In the supervisor pattern, a central orchestrator agent receives user requests and delegates tasks to specialized sub-agents (e.g., planner, researcher, critic). The supervisor manages the workflow sequence, passes outputs between agents, handles revision loops when quality checks fail, and compiles the final response. Each sub-agent has its own system prompt, tool access, and focused responsibility.

input: What are the key differences between BM25 and dense vector search for document retrieval?
expected_output: BM25 is a sparse retrieval method based on term frequency and inverse document frequency, excelling at exact keyword matching. Dense vector search uses neural embeddings to capture semantic similarity, handling synonyms and paraphrases better. BM25 is faster and needs no training, while dense search requires an embedding model. Hybrid approaches combining both methods with cross-encoder reranking typically achieve the best retrieval quality.

input: Explain the role of cross-encoder reranking in a hybrid retrieval pipeline.
expected_output: Cross-encoder reranking is a second-stage retrieval step where a model jointly encodes the query and each candidate document to produce a relevance score. Unlike bi-encoders that encode query and documents independently, cross-encoders capture fine-grained query-document interactions. In a hybrid pipeline, initial candidates from BM25 and dense search are merged, then reranked by the cross-encoder to select the most relevant passages for the LLM context.

input: RAG vs fine-tuning для покращення якості відповідей LLM
expected_output: RAG та fine-tuning - два підходи до покращення LLM. RAG додає зовнішні знання під час генерації, що дозволяє легко оновлювати дані без перенавчання. Fine-tuning адаптує ваги моделі на специфічних даних, покращуючи стиль та формат відповідей. RAG краще для фактичних знань, fine-tuning - для адаптації поведінки. Оптимальний підхід часто поєднує обидва методи.

Knowledge retrieval encompasses methods for finding and extracting relevant information from document collections. Key approaches include sparse retrieval (BM25/TF-IDF), dense retrieval (vector embeddings), and hybrid methods. Modern systems combine multiple retrieval stages with reranking for optimal results.

input: Provide an exhaustive analysis of every possible embedding model architecture, every retrieval algorithm ever published, all chunking methods, all reranking approaches, every RAG framework, and all evaluation benchmarks for information retrieval systems.
expected_output: A comprehensive overview of embedding architectures includes BERT-based bi-encoders, sentence transformers, and instruction-tuned models. Key retrieval algorithms span BM25, DPR, ColBERT, and SPLADE. Common chunking methods include fixed-size, recursive, and semantic approaches. Reranking uses cross-encoders or listwise models. Major RAG frameworks include LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Haystack. Standard benchmarks include BEIR, MTEB, and MS MARCO.

input: What is the optimal chunk_overlap parameter when using RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with chunk_size=512 for technical documentation about transformer architectures?
expected_output: For technical documentation about transformers with chunk_size=512, a chunk_overlap of 50-100 tokens (10-20% of chunk size) is recommended. This preserves context across chunk boundaries without excessive redundancy. For highly interconnected content like architecture descriptions, leaning toward 15-20% overlap helps maintain coherence of cross-referenced concepts.

input: How do LangChain and LlamaIndex differ in their approach to building RAG applications?
expected_output: LangChain provides a general-purpose framework with modular chains, agents, and tool abstractions for building LLM applications. LlamaIndex focuses specifically on data ingestion and retrieval, offering specialized data connectors, index structures, and query engines. LangChain excels in complex agent workflows while LlamaIndex offers deeper retrieval customization. Both support similar LLM providers and can be used together.
